record.original_question: Given a string group generated by involutions, determine the minimal string C-groups that cover it.

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Given a string group generated by involutions, determine the minimal string C-groups that cover it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group and let $S = (\rho_0, \rho_1, \ldots, \rho_{n-1})$ be an ordered generating set of $G$ such that each $\rho_i$ is an involution and the involutions satisfy the string commuting property: $(\rho_i \rho_j)^2 = 1$ whenever $|i-j| \ge 2$. Such a pair $(G,S)$ is called a string group generated by involutions (sggi).

An sggi $(G,S)$ is called a string C-group if, in addition, it satisfies the intersection property: for every $I, J \subseteq \{0, 1, \ldots, n-1\}$,
$$\langle \rho_i : i \in I\rangle \cap \langle \rho_j : j \in J\rangle = \langle \rho_k : k \in I \cap J\rangle.$$

Given two sggis $(G,S)$ and $(\widetilde G, \widetilde S)$ of the same rank $n$, we say that $(\widetilde G,\widetilde S)$ covers $(G,S)$ if the map $\widetilde \rho_i \mapsto \rho_i$ extends to a surjective group homomorphism $\widetilde G \to G$. A cover $(\widetilde G, \widetilde S)$ of $(G,S)$ that is a string C-group is called minimal if no proper quotient of $(\widetilde G,\widetilde S)$ (other than $(G,S)$ itself if it happens to be a string C-group) covers $(G,S)$ and is a string C-group.

Problem: Given an arbitrary string group generated by involutions $(G,S)$, determine all minimal string C-groups that cover $(G,S)$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this problem was located. Related work develops the theory of string C-groups and computational tools (e.g., the SGGI Magma package) for sggis, and constructions of minimal common covers exist in special cases for regular polyhedra, but a general determination of minimal string C-group covers of an arbitrary sggi does not appear in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: SGGI: A Magma package to compute with String Groups Generated by Involutions
status_evidence.snippet: A Magma package to compute with SGGIs: String Groups Generated by Involutions.
status_evidence.claim: Computational tools exist for investigating sggis but no general theorem determines minimal string C-group covers.

status_evidence.title: Self-Dual, Self-Petrie Covers of Regular Polyhedra
status_evidence.snippet: Mixing operation provides a natural way to build the minimal common cover of two polyhedra.
status_evidence.claim: Minimal covers are studied only in special cases (e.g., self-dual, self-Petrie covers); a general answer for sggis is not given.
